text:
Detroit and Florida meet in Sunrise with both teams at 3-2-0 in their last five and both thin at the top of the lineup. The Red Wings fell 5-4 to St. Louis on Saturday after blowing a two-goal lead, and they're missing Dylan Larkin (suspension), Albert Johansson and Mason Appleton. Alex DeBrincat has moved onto Larkin's spot beside Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson. The Panthers have won three straight without Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov, with Carter Verhaeghe now on a line with Sam Reinhart and Matthew Tkachuk's brother Brady, and Anton Lundell scoring three in the 5-2 win over Winnipeg.

The teams are close at five on five. Detroit has taken 54% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and Florida 55%, and our model projects 3.10 goals for DET and 3.02 for FLA. Special teams are the matchup to watch: Detroit's power play creates 0.83 expected goals a game against a Florida penalty kill allowing 0.89, and the Panthers take 5.6 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Daniil Tarasov (DET) is +5.1 goals saved above expected this season, against +1.3 for Jacob Markstrom (FLA). Last year both were below zero. Tarasov also returns to Sunrise for the first time since leaving the Panthers.

Raymond is worth watching: he has eight points in his last five games, as CBS Sports noted, and we give him a 66% chance at a point. Arvidsson (37% to score) and DeBrincat (36%) lead Detroit in goal odds. For Florida, Reinhart sits at 35% to score, and Seth Jones, whom NHL.com wrote "piled up the points in October," has a 59% chance at a point.
